name: Chicago Community Bond Fund
mission: The Chicago Community Bond Fund (CCBF) pays bond for people charged with crimes in Cook County, Illinois. Through a revolving fund, CCBF supports individuals whose communities cannot afford to pay the bonds themselves and who have been impacted by structural violence.
theoryOfChange: By paying bond, CCBF restores the presumption of innocence before trial and enables recipients to remain free while fighting their cases. People free on bond have better case outcomes than people are locked up.

rich_narrative.summary: The Chicago Community Bond Fund faces significant operational and financial challenges that limit its baseline rating. In FY2024, the organization reported a severe financial deficit where expenses reached 5.0 times its revenue, drawing down <cite id="2">$510,635 in FY2024 revenue</cite> against significantly higher expenditures. Furthermore, revenue contracted by 32% from FY2023 to FY2024, moving from $751,883 down to $510,635. While the charity maintains <cite id="1">a 96/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite> and operates with <cite id="1">a low fundraising efficiency of $0.08 per $1 raised</cite>, the lack of published cost-per-beneficiary metrics and the primary focus on general legal advocacy result in a low alignment for specific faith-based donor priorities.
